metadata.note: JWT mount accessor not documented in provided docs; canonical operation absent for target protocol.
No auth mount disable endpoint documented in provided docs; using provider deletion as closest documented cleanup for OIDC provider resources.

oidc_jwt.description: Successful JWT/OIDC auth uses the configured user_claim value as the Identity entity alias name.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt role docs: user_claim is used as the name for the Identity entity alias created due to a successful login
oidc_jwt.note: Display-name or alias differences may reflect configured claim selection rather than identity confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault token lookup-self display_name includes an auth-path-derived prefix before the user identity value.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/token lookup-self example shows display_name like ldap2-tesla
oidc_jwt.note: The prefix is platform metadata from the auth mount path, not necessarily an identity mismatch.

oidc_jwt.description: Reusing the same upstream JWT for multiple login attempts is not documented as prevented by jti tracking.
oidc_jwt.source: JWT auth docs describe signature and claim validation but no jti replay cache
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report replay_same_token as a vulnerability for plain JWT bearer auth unless a stronger freshness mechanism was explicitly configured elsewhere.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's JWT login documentation describes signature and claim validation but does not document jti tracking or one-time JWT consumption. Reusing the same valid JWT may succeed repeatedly by design for stateless JWT verification.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt JWT login and role docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay_same_token or missing jti tracking as a vulnerability for plain JWT auth without additional replay-binding features.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault OIDC provider requires PKCE for public clients and only optionally supports it for confidential clients.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC provider client docs and token endpoint docs
oidc_jwt.note: A missing code_verifier rejection for public clients is expected hardening behavior; confidential-client behavior differs by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault public OIDC clients do not have a client secret and must use PKCE for the authorization code flow.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client
oidc_jwt.note: Token exchange without code_verifier for public clients should fail by design.

oidc_jwt.description: A provider with empty allowed_client_ids allows no clients.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC provider docs: If empty, no clients are allowed
oidc_jwt.note: Authorization failures may be caused by provider allowlisting, not token validation bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: An OIDC client with no assignments allows no Vault entities to authenticate through the client.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC client docs: By default, no Vault entities are allowed
oidc_jwt.note: Provider authorization failures can be expected until allow_all or explicit assignments are configured.

oidc_jwt.description: When group_policy_application_mode is set to any, group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-namespace policy reach in this mode is by design and should not be flagged as escalation.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault OIDC clients deny authentication for all Vault entities unless assignments are configured; the built-in allow_all assignment is required to permit all entities.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client
oidc_jwt.note: Authentication failures through a client with no assignments are expected by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's OIDC provider does not support request or request_uri parameters at the authorization endpoint.
oidc_jwt.note: Unsigned request object tests are not applicable; rejection is by design.

oidc_jwt.constraint: configure_jwt_validation requires exactly one trust source: set ONE AND ONLY ONE of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Do not set multiple sources in the same test, or setup is invalid and I1 results are meaningless.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless the test intentionally checks behavior when issuer binding is omitted. Without bound_issuer, Vault does not compare the JWT iss claim, so forged-issuer tests can appear to 'pass' trivially because issuer validation was never configured.

When jwks_pairs is used in configure_jwt_validation, bound_issuer cannot be configured. Do not generate issuer-enforcement tests against a jwks_pairs setup; use oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys instead.

Every JWT/OIDC role requires at least one bound value to be set. The docs state 'At least one of the bound values must be set.' Do not create unconstrained roles for baseline tests; setup will fail or be invalid.

For JWT roles with an aud claim, bound_audiences is required and must match at least one JWT aud value. For I5 audience tests, include a control token whose aud matches the configured bound_audiences; otherwise a failed attack login may just reflect missing required audience setup.

bound_subject supports EXACT string matching only. There is no companion bound_subject_type parameter. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally, not as patterns. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple different sub values to authenticate to the same role, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting it to '*'.

bound_audiences is exact list-membership matching only; the docs provide no companion type parameter. Do not use wildcard audience values. For cross-provider or multi-client tests where different aud values must pass the same role, either omit bound_audiences only when the JWT under test has no aud claim, or create separate roles with explicit audiences.

bound_claims matching mode is controlled by bound_claims_type. Default value 'string' means literal exact matching; 'glob' enables '*' wildcard matching. For I4 multi-identity tests, if multiple different claim values must pass the same constraint, set bound_claims_type=glob with an intentional pattern, or omit the constraint entirely. Do NOT set bound_claims values to '*' while leaving bound_claims_type at default 'string' because only the literal string '*' will match.

bound_claims accepts expected values of string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. Because the default bound_claims_type is 'string' and values are treated as literals, non-string JWT claim values may be rejected rather than coerced. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type to 'glob' so numeric claim values are coerced to strings rather than rejected outright.

groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. For I4 type-confusion tests, distinguish between a JWT groups claim encoded as a string versus an array: the documented valid type is list-of-strings only, so a string value may be rejected rather than mapped. Do not treat rejection of string-typed groups as an identity-collision bug.

user_claim must resolve to a STRING, and it becomes the identity alias name created on successful login. For I4 tests, choose a stable string claim (commonly sub) and remember that alias collisions are security-relevant because multiple authenticated entities can bind to the same alias name.

If user_claim_json_pointer is false (default), user_claim is interpreted literally, not as a JSON pointer. For tests that reference nested claims, explicitly set user_claim_json_pointer=true; otherwise the role will look for a claim whose literal name contains slashes and the test will fail for setup reasons.
clock_skew_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 60 seconds, NOT strict zero; value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 means no skew allowance.

expiration_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, NOT strict zero; value -1 disables this extra leeway. For I2 expired_token tests, do not set expiration_leeway=0 expecting immediate expiry enforcement; use -1 for strict behavior or account for the default 150-second grace window.

not_before_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, NOT strict zero; value -1 disables this extra leeway. For I2 future_token/nbf tests, do not set not_before_leeway=0 expecting strict enforcement; use -1 for strict behavior or place nbf sufficiently far in the future beyond the default grace window.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid token alongside the ATTACK login. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED on the attack token cannot be distinguished from broken JWT trust configuration, missing bound values, or malformed role setup.

token_num_uses limits how many API calls can be made with the issued Vault session token, and EVERY authenticated API call consumes a use, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-bound verification calls are present.

For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role and then uses the mount's default_role. To test default-role coherence correctly, the baseline and attack logins must both omit role explicitly; specifying role bypasses the default-role behavior entirely.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, update the SAME auth mount config via configure_jwt_validation/modify_role_config and then retry login_with_jwt. A valid test checks whether NEW logins immediately honor the updated trust anchor; it is not an inconsistency if tokens issued before the config change remain valid as Vault tokens after login.

For I3 jwt_role_config_tighten_reauth tests, modify_role_config must NARROW constraints (for example add bound_claims or tighten bound_audiences). Removing constraints or emptying bound_claims broadens access and cannot be used as a tightening oracle.

OIDC auth_url/callback flow is session-bound by state, nonce, and optional client_nonce. For I3 flow-coherence tests, preserve the exact state and nonce returned in the generated auth_url and send the same client_nonce to callback if one was used at auth_url time. Mixing values across sessions is expected to fail and should be interpreted as correct binding, not a bug.

Vault's OIDC auth_url endpoint returns a generated upstream authorization URL rather than acting as the authorization endpoint itself. Do not apply RFC9101 request-object or alg=none tests to /v1/auth/{mount}/oidc/auth_url; that endpoint only constructs a URL and the provided docs do not document request JWT support there.

For Vault as an OIDC relying party, the callback requires state, nonce, and code, and client_nonce must match if supplied earlier. For I2 replay and I3 state-swap tests, treat nonce/state/client_nonce mismatches as expected flow rejection, not identity confusion.
Vault OIDC provider authorization endpoint requires scope to include 'openid'. Tests against the provider's /authorize endpoint that omit openid are invalid setup, not security failures.

Vault OIDC provider client_type has security-relevant PKCE semantics: public clients MUST use PKCE and confidential clients MAY use PKCE. For OIDC provider flow tests, do not interpret missing code_verifier enforcement on confidential clients as a bug if PKCE was not required for that client type; but for public clients, code_verifier is required at the token endpoint.

Vault OIDC provider redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authentication request. For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, a mismatch rejection is expected behavior; ensure the control flow uses an exact configured redirect URI.

Vault OIDC provider assignments default to allowing NO Vault entities to authenticate through the client. To create a working control flow, configure the client with an assignment such as the built-in allow_all or an assignment containing the target entity/group. Otherwise authorization failures at /authorize or /token are setup errors, not I5 findings.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids on the provider defaults to allowing NO clients when empty; '*' allows all clients. For cross-client/provider audience-style tests, ensure the provider and key/client configuration explicitly allow the client under test, or failures may be caused by provider-side allowlisting rather than token validation.

OIDC provider access_token_ttl and id_token_ttl are independent client settings. For freshness tests against provider-issued tokens, use the configured TTLs rather than assuming a platform default, and remember that session_token for API calls is the access_token, not the id_token.

identity/oidc/introspect validates Vault-issued OIDC ID tokens, not Vault auth mount session tokens and not arbitrary upstream JWTs. Do not use introspect_token as an oracle for login_with_jwt acceptance or for Vault client_token freshness.
KV v2 verify_read_secret MUST use the /data/ path segment. Using /v1/{mount}/{path} without /data/ hits the wrong API shape and returns 404 for setup reasons, not authorization reasons.

KV v2 engine config max_versions has sentinel semantics: value 0 means keep the default 10 versions, NOT zero versions. delete_version_after has sentinel semantics: value '0s' means no automatic deletion timer. Never assume zero disables storage or causes immediate deletion.

For KV v2 CAS tests, options.cas=0 means create only if the key does not yet exist; it is not a generic 'disable CAS' value. On soft-deleted keys, writes still require cas to match the current version because version history remains. Do not misinterpret CAS failures as authorization failures.

Group policy application mode can change authorization semantics globally. Default mode is within_namespace_hierarchy; mode 'any' applies group policies regardless of namespace hierarchy. For I5 group-policy-escalation tests, record the current /sys/config/group-policy-application mode and do not flag cross-namespace group policy application as a bug when the mode is explicitly set to 'any'.

Entity alias names are security-sensitive. Vault docs explicitly warn that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby gain all of its privileges. For I4 collision tests, alias reuse is a real attack surface; do not auto-deduplicate or normalize away alias-name collisions in the oracle.
Exactly one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, and jwt_validation_pubkeys MUST be set in configure_jwt_validation. Do not send multiple trust-anchor sources in the same config.
bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. For issuer-validation tests, do NOT use jwks_pairs if the test requires bound_issuer enforcement.
For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer. If omitted, Vault has no configured issuer value to compare against, so issuer-mismatch tests are invalid.

JWT role creation requires at least one bound value to be set. Tests must include at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims (or other documented bound values) or role creation/setup is invalid.

For jwt roles that contain an aud claim (typical case), bound_audiences is required and the JWT aud must match at least one configured audience. For audience-mismatch tests, first run a control login with a matching aud.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only. There is no companion type parameter for bound_subject. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting a wildcard.

bound_claims matching is controlled by bound_claims_type. Default 'string' mode treats values as literals and requires exact matches; 'glob' enables '*' wildcard matching. For wildcard tests, set bound_claims_type=glob explicitly.

For I5 numeric coercion tests on bound_claims, set bound_claims_type to glob, not the default string, so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching rather than rejected outright by exact literal string handling.

bound_claims accepts expected values as string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. Because docs do not specify float/integer cross-type behavior, the fuzzer SHOULD test numeric coercion explicitly (e.g. bound integer N vs JWT float N+0.7) to detect silent truncation or coercion.

user_claim must resolve to a STRING claim value. groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. Type-confusion tests that send scalar vs array values may fail by design due to type requirements rather than revealing an identity-collision bug.

If user_claim uses JSON pointer syntax, user_claim_json_pointer MUST be set to true. Otherwise Vault interprets the value literally as a claim name, causing setup/login failures unrelated to the security property under test.

token_num_uses limits every API call made with the resulting Vault session token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read, the minimum safe value is 2; use 3 if an additional entity lookup is performed.

OIDC auth_url returns a Vault-generated auth_url rather than acting as a standard /authorize endpoint. The fuzzer must treat this as a flow bootstrap step and preserve the returned state/nonce values for the callback; do not synthesize your own callback parameters.

OIDC callback requires state, nonce, and code, and optionally client_nonce matching the prior auth_url request. For I3 flow-coherence tests, reuse or swap any of these only intentionally; mismatches are expected rejections, not bugs.
If client_nonce is supplied to auth_url, the same client_nonce MUST be supplied to callback. This is an explicit session-binding value and should be preserved for valid control flows.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request and callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC response type 'id_token' may only be used when oidc_response_mode is form_post. Do not configure incompatible combinations when testing OIDC flow behavior.

If using Vault namespaces and oidc_response_mode=form_post, namespace_in_state should be set to false. Otherwise redirect/callback behavior may differ for namespace reasons unrelated to the tested invariant.

For jwt_default_role_change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role only when configure_jwt_validation has default_role set. If default_role is unset, omitting role is invalid setup, not a security failure.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids has permissive sentinel semantics: empty means NO clients are allowed; '*' means ALL clients are allowed. Do not confuse empty with wildcard. For cross-client authorization tests, choose explicitly between deny-all and allow-all.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider Create or update a provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC client assignments default to deny-all: by default, no Vault entities are allowed to authenticate through the client. To permit authentication in tests, configure assignments explicitly or use the built-in allow_all assignment.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC client redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authentication request. Redirect URI mismatch rejections are by design and must not be interpreted as flow-coherence bugs.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: Vault OIDC provider public clients MUST use PKCE for the authorization code flow; confidential clients may use PKCE optionally. Tests that omit code_verifier for public clients should expect rejection by design.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client client_type and provider token endpoint

oidc_jwt.constraint: Vault OIDC provider token endpoint supports only grant_type=authorization_code in the documented endpoint. Do not attempt RFC 8693 token exchange against this endpoint based on the provided docs.

OIDC provider discovery explicitly reports request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run request-object or request_uri attack variants against Vault's documented OIDC provider endpoint; unsupported features will fail by design.

For OIDC RP validation tests against Vault's JWT/OIDC auth method, preserve and validate nonce across the auth_url and callback flow. The docs make nonce a required callback parameter and client_nonce an optional additional binding value.

Identity alias names can be reused across multiple authenticated entities, which can cause privilege sharing. When manually creating aliases for test setup, use unique alias names per entity and mount to avoid false I4/I5 findings caused by documented alias reuse risk.

External identity groups should be used with group aliases for external JWT/OIDC groups. Manual member_entity_ids on groups can change effective permissions and confound group-claim authorization tests.

Group policy application mode can be globally set to 'within_namespace_hierarchy' or 'any'. Cross-namespace group-policy escalation tests must first read this global mode; 'any' intentionally relaxes namespace restrictions and can otherwise look like an authorization bug.

KV v2 read paths require the /data/ segment. If the target secret engine is KV v2, verify_read_secret and seed_protected_resource must use /v1/{engine}/data/{path}; using /v1/{engine}/{path} will hit KV v1 semantics and produce misleading 404/permission results.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless you intentionally test the unbound case. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault will not compare the JWT iss claim and issuer-mismatch tests become meaningless.
bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. Do not use jwks_pairs for issuer-enforcement tests because it prevents configuring the issuer check you are trying to test.

create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. A role with no bound constraints is invalid setup. Ensure at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims is present when creating JWT/OIDC roles.

For JWT roles, bound_audiences is required when the JWT contains an aud claim (the typical case) and at least one configured audience must match one of the JWT aud values. For I5 audience tests, do not omit bound_audiences unless you are explicitly testing the unbound configuration.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only; there is no companion type parameter. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally, not as patterns. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple sub values to pass the same role, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting it to a wildcard.

bound_claims supports two matching modes controlled by bound_claims_type. Default bound_claims_type='string' means literal exact matching; 'glob' enables wildcard matching with '*'. For I4 multi-identity tests, do not set exact-match bound_claims entries to '*' unless you intend to match the literal string '*'. Use bound_claims_type='glob' for wildcard tests or omit the constraint entirely.

For I5 numeric coercion tests on bound_claims, set bound_claims_type='glob' rather than the default 'string'. The docs state default string mode treats values as literals and must match exactly, while glob mode interprets values as globs; use glob mode so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings instead of being rejected outright.

bound_claims accepts expected values as string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. Because the docs do not fully specify cross-type comparison semantics, the fuzzer SHOULD test numeric coercion explicitly: configure a numeric bound_claims value N, then send a JWT claim with float N+0.7 and observe whether Vault truncates/coerces silently. Use bound_claims_type='glob' if needed to avoid outright type rejection.

user_claim and bound_claims keys can use JSON Pointer syntax only when configured accordingly. user_claim_json_pointer defaults to false, so a slash-containing user_claim is treated literally unless user_claim_json_pointer=true. For tests targeting nested claims, set the JSON pointer mode explicitly or setup will not reference the intended claim.

Numeric sentinel semantics for JWT leeway fields: clock_skew_leeway value 0 means use default 60 seconds, not strict zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. expiration_leeway value 0 means use default 150 seconds, not immediate expiry; value -1 disables extra leeway. not_before_leeway value 0 means use default 150 seconds; value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict checking.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, account for Vault's default leeway behavior. A token with exp or nbf only slightly outside the current time may still be accepted because expiration_leeway/not_before_leeway default to 150s and clock_skew_leeway defaults to 60s when set to 0. To test strict freshness, set the relevant leeway fields to -1 or move timestamps well beyond the default buffers.

For I2 token-freshness tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT alongside the ATTACK login. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED on an expired/future token cannot be distinguished from broken JWKS/issuer/role setup.

JWT replay with the same bearer JWT is not documented as one-time and Vault JWT auth is a stateless verifier. Do not treat successful reuse of the same JWT as an I2 vulnerability by itself unless the tested scenario adds an explicit one-time property outside standard JWT validation.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, update configure_jwt_validation trust material (jwks_url or jwt_validation_pubkeys) and then perform a NEW login. A valid test asserts that a JWT signed by the old key is rejected after reconfiguration; it is not a bug that tokens already issued by Vault before the change remain valid until their own TTL expires.

For I3 jwt_bound_issuer_enforce tests, reconfigure bound_issuer and then perform a NEW login with the old issuer token. The test must verify immediate effect on subsequent authentications, not retroactive invalidation of already-issued Vault tokens.

For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, omit the role parameter on login_with_jwt so the mount's default_role is actually exercised. If role is sent explicitly, changing default_role will have no effect and the test will be invalid.

For I3 jwt_role_config_tighten_reauth tests, modify_role_config must NARROW constraints or permissions (for example add bound_claims or tighten bound_audiences). Removing constraints or emptying bound_claims broadens access and is not a valid tightening test.

OIDC provider authorization endpoint requires scope to include 'openid' and only supports response_type='code'. Do not attempt implicit or hybrid flow variants against this provider; failures would be by design.

Vault OIDC provider discovery advertises request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do not run oidc_request_object_alg_none tests against this provider authorization endpoint because request JWT objects are not supported and rejection is by design.

OIDC provider token endpoint only supports grant_type='authorization_code'. Do not attempt RFC 8693 token exchange or other grant types at this endpoint; such failures are expected and not evidence of audience or scope enforcement bugs.

For OIDC code flow tests with public clients, PKCE is required: create_application with client_type='public' MUST be paired with code_challenge at authorize and code_verifier at token exchange. Missing PKCE for public clients should be treated as expected rejection, not a flow-coherence bug.

For OIDC code flow tests with confidential clients, client authentication method matters. The token endpoint accepts client_secret_basic via Authorization header or client_secret_post via form fields; public clients use none. Ensure the exchange method matches the client type or failures will reflect bad client auth, not the property under test.

For OIDC replay protection tests, send and track nonce explicitly in start_oidc_auth. The docs strongly encourage nonce and state it is returned in the ID token; omitting nonce weakens replay-oriented tests and prevents validation of nonce binding.

OIDC token endpoint redirect_uri must exactly match the redirect_uri used when the authorization code was generated, and client redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each auth request. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, ensure the baseline uses an exact match first; otherwise failures may be simple misconfiguration.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids semantics: empty means NO clients are allowed; '*' means all clients are allowed. Do not interpret empty as unrestricted. For cross-client authorization tests, configure allowed_client_ids deliberately or the provider may reject all clients by design.

OIDC client assignments semantics: by default, no Vault entities are allowed to authenticate through a client. To allow all entities, include the built-in assignment 'allow_all', or create a specific assignment referencing entity_ids/group_ids. If omitted, login failures are expected authorization denials, not authentication bugs.

OIDC client_type, key, and some provider/client properties are immutable after creation according to the docs ('cannot be modified after creation'). For I3 config-change tests, create fresh resources when changing immutable fields instead of expecting in-place updates to take effect.

OIDC client TTL fields id_token_ttl and access_token_ttl accept int or duration and default to 24h. Tests that expect rapid expiry must explicitly lower these values; otherwise long-lived tokens are by design.

Identity alias cardinality matters: Vault docs warn that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby gain all of its privileges. For I4 collision tests involving manual alias management, use unique alias names per entity unless you are intentionally testing alias reuse/collision behavior.

Each entity can only have one alias per mount accessor, and entity merges fail on conflicting aliases unless conflicting_alias_ids_to_keep is provided and only one from-entity is merged. Do not misinterpret merge failures under same-mount alias conflicts as security protections failing; they are documented identity-store constraints.

External identity groups should be used with group aliases for external auth sources. For JWT/OIDC groups_claim mapping tests, create_identity_group with type='external' and map the external group name via create_group_alias using the auth mount accessor. Manual member_entity_ids on such groups can produce misleading authorization results.

Group policy application mode affects cross-namespace authorization. Default mode is within_namespace_hierarchy; mode 'any' relaxes this and applies group policies regardless of namespace hierarchy. For I5 group-policy-escalation tests, record the current /sys/config/group-policy-application mode because cross-namespace policy reach may be by design.

KV v2 verify_read_secret and seed_protected_resource paths MUST include /data/. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and will return 404 on KV v2 mounts, causing false negatives in access tests.

KV v2 CAS semantics: write options.cas=0 means create only if the key does not yet exist; it does NOT mean 'no check'. If engine or key metadata has cas_required=true, writes must include a matching current version. For setup, avoid cas=0 on existing or soft-deleted keys unless you intentionally test CAS enforcement.

KV v2 numeric sentinel semantics: engine config max_versions=0 means use the default of 10 versions, not zero versions retained. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic deletion delay is configured. Do not assume zero disables version retention or causes immediate deletion.

Session-use budget analysis: token_num_uses/num_uses style limits on issued Vault tokens count EVERY API call made with that token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_entity_details before verify_read_secret. If the fuzzer needs both a verification call and a protected-resource read, minimum safe value is at least 2; use at least 3 if an additional entity lookup is included.
